svg.title: Database 2PC versus TCC: lock lifetimes during a wallet transfer
svg.desc: Two stacked panels adapt chapter 27 wallet timelines. Both show a successful one-dollar transfer from account A in Database A to account C in Database C. Time moves left to right in each panel. The upper database two-phase commit panel shows both account balance row locks surviving prepare and ending when each database commits its prepared transaction, before its acknowledgement is sent. The lower Try-Confirm/Cancel panel shows A locked only during its Try local transaction and C locked only during its Confirm local transaction. A blue span separately shows the committed business reservation remaining pending between A's Try commit and A's Confirm completion. Only balance row locks are illustrated; phase and reservation records can require other brief local locks. NOP means no balance change. This is a success path; rollback also releases a prepared transaction's locks, while TCC Cancel uses a new local transaction.
svg.text: Database 2PC vs TCC: when do the database locks end?
Successful $1 transfer: A to C. Read both timelines left to right; durations are illustrative.
Business reservation (separate from a DB lock)
Database 2PC — prepared updates keep their locks
Updates stay uncommitted through Prepare. Each database unlocks when its own COMMIT completes.
TCC — local commits release locks between phases
Try commits a reservation; Confirm uses new local transactions to finish the transfer.
Red spans show account balance row locks. Phase records may need other brief locks. NOP = no balance change.
Abort path: 2PC unlocks on ROLLBACK of the prepared transaction; TCC Cancel releases its hold in a new local transaction.
